citation.authors: Liangyue Cao, Amanda Hosking, Michael Kouparitsas, Damian Mullaly, Xavier Rimmer, Qun Shi, Wallace Stark and Sebastian Wende
citation.title: Understanding the economy-wide efficiency and incidence of major Australian taxes
citation.locator: Table 2 'Company income tax — Marginal excess burden comparison', p. 22 (PDF p. 25); text p. 20 (PDF p. 23)

entries.quote: Table 2: Company income tax — Marginal excess burden comparison … Baseline 0.50 … Low rent share 1.35 … Low elasticity 0.20 … An increase in the company income tax rate implies an overall welfare loss of around 50 cents per dollar of net revenue (Chart 4).
entries.derivation: Value = the baseline (0.50). Low and high = the lowest and highest of the paper's sensitivity cases in Table 2: 0.20 (low consumption–leisure substitution elasticity) and 1.35 (low rent share).
entries.notes: Static CGE model of a small open economy; long run. A company tax change costed in C3 cannot also be the funding tax (overlap rule O-5). KPMG's estimates are in c11.meb-company-income.kpmg.

citation.locator: Table 3 'Flat personal income tax — Marginal excess burden comparison', column 'Labour income tax MEB ($)', p. 32 (PDF p. 35); text p. 31 (PDF p. 34)

entries.quote: Table 3: Flat personal income tax — Marginal excess burden comparison … Baseline 0.16 0.21 … Low elasticity 0.00 0.00 … High elasticity 0.35 0.48 … The high sensitivity estimate results from a high elasticity of substitution between consumption and leisure.
entries.derivation: Value = the baseline (0.21). Low and high = the lowest and highest sensitivity cases in Table 3: 0.00 (no consumption–leisure substitution) and 0.48 (high substitution).
entries.notes: At higher effective tax rates the MEB is higher: 0.27 at the 2011-12 average tax rate and 0.32 at the average marginal rate (Table 3, rows above the sensitivities).

entries.quote: Table 5: Broad-based land tax — Marginal excess burden comparison … Baseline -0.10 … Low foreign ownership 0.00 … High foreign ownership -0.20
entries.derivation: Value = the baseline (−0.10). Low and high = the lowest and highest sensitivity cases in Table 5: −0.20 (high foreign ownership) and 0.00 (low foreign ownership).
entries.notes: The paper: "The baseline negative marginal excess burden reported here is driven by the assumption of foreign ownership of land" (p. 44).
